# SOC-C15 extraction notes (A2)

Text: pdftotext -layout of the supplied PDF, saved in _text/full.txt. Page numbers are printed page numbers (= PDF page numbers).

## Scope
- Headline sources: Executive summary, Key findings and Recommendations (p.7-10); Implications and recommendations, including Answers to the central evaluation questions and Recommendations (p.58-62).
- Repeated claims (rule 11): the ES and the conclusions repeat most claims in near-identical words; one row lists both locations. Where the conclusions add a separable assertion, it has its own row (C11, C17, C18, C20-C22, C26, C36, C39).
- Research agenda excluded (rule 6): ES "Evaluation" p.10 and conclusions "Evaluation" p.61-62 (longer longitudinal evaluation, tracking of individual women, optimum length of 18 months, earlier intervention, care leavers, a man-centred equivalent, gaps in service provision). No rows proposed.
- Not headline: the closing sentence of Appendix F (p.84, "Pause is highly likely to produce significant cost savings over time") and the description of Pause's mission (p.13).

## Rows proposed
- findings: 52 (N 23, Q 29; F28 and F30 are N made from Q). transformations: 4 (2 crosses_strand yes, 2 no). claims: 39. relations: 15 (covers 10, backs 5, clashes 0). decisions: header only.

## Look at first
1. Joint claims (4): C5, C6 (fit confirm; the ES sentence itself names "Qualitative data and data from CMFs"), C17 (expand), C19 (confirm). No claim reaches both strands only through a transformation: F28 and F30 (counted interview responses, crosses_strand yes) are not used by any headline claim.
2. C1 ("Findings from qualitative and quantitative data suggest [...] positive and significant impact"). The claim names both strands but cites no findings at that point; A2 applied rule 2 (empty rests_on, covers C5-C14). If A1 prefers to trace it through the claims it covers, C1 is joint.
3. C12 (significant improvements in confidence and self-worth, "Qualitative data show"). Rests on interview and case-study findings (F42, F52). The CMF self-esteem measure on the closest construct gives a mixed picture: of 45 women, 44% improved, 40% decreased (F14, p.35). The authors do not link F14 to C12 and do not report it in the headline sections. Under rule 3 F14 is not in rests_on; fit recorded single-strand. This is the main point where a quantitative result sits beside a qualitative headline claim without being used; the reviewer may want it recorded as a note on discord.
4. C6 ("associated with improved outcomes for some women"). The N part is that 6 of 12 women who reduced drinking and 2 of 9 who left problematic drug use had been in treatment (F17, F18; p.34 "In some cases, these reductions occurred while women were engaging with alcohol and substance misuse services"). No association test is reported. The Q part is F35 (p.45).
5. C17 (substance misuse illustration, conclusions p.59). No explicit pointer to findings; rests_on proposed under rule 8 (reductions = F17, F18; mechanisms = Q process findings). If A1 treats it as an illustration without findings, rests_on becomes empty and C17 is not joint.
6. C19 (cohort needs). Restates the baseline CMF results (F7-F11) and the baseline interview theme on grief (F22) on the same measures (rule 8). "anxiety" rests on the diagnosis counts in F7.
7. C11 (conclusions summary of housing, alcohol, drugs, DV). Proposed with rests_on via rule 8 rather than as a summary claim with covers relations to C7-C10. "safeguarded themselves against violence and abuse" goes beyond F16 (no incident reported at the latest time-point); F39 (some women exited violent relationships, p.47-48) bears on it but is not linked by the authors.
8. Empty rests_on (rule 3), with candidate findings:
   - C3 (pregnancies likely to result in removals): candidate F6 (368 removals, 89.1% care proceedings). The evaluation question is about removals; the models measure pregnancies, and the CBA uses pregnancies as a proxy (p.55).
   - C16 (mechanisms operating simultaneously): backed by C17; p.42 ("problems in one area can impact negatively on each of the rest") and F35 bear on it.
   - C18 (pause in pregnancies an important enabler): "evidence from this evaluation suggests" without a pointer; candidates F3, F13 (pregnancy-free period achieved), F27/F28 (welcome break from pregnancy). No finding shows the period enabling other changes.
   - C22 (problems compounded): backed by C20, C21 ("therefore").
9. Recommendations C25-C39 rest on the "lessons" from interviews with Pause professionals (p.52-54) and process findings, under rule 8. Weak matches: C27 (F37 only says the flexibility was deliberate), C34 (F33 names mental health, housing, probation as slow to change; substance misuse services are not named there), C37 (F46 is about expected induction, not replication).
10. C15 lists three mechanisms in one assertion; not split (rule 5). The ES calls it "Analysis of qualitative data"; the chapter (p.42) says the theory of change draws "on findings from both the impact and the process elements", so A1 may judge whether any N finding belongs in rests_on.

## Interface points (not transformations)
- Rule 9: the CMF was "designed by the evaluation team with input from Pause professionals" (p.16); its findings stay N roots.
- Qualitative findings used to interpret N results: increases in DV disclosures (p.36-37), higher risk drinking (p.38) and drug use (p.39, fn 17) are read in light of the qualitative finding that trust developed over the first months; Appendix F (p.79) excludes increases from the cost model on the same ground. No new finding is produced, so A2 did not record a transformation.
- p.45: contraception figures (F13) and the interview count (F28) are used together to argue that the model encouraged uptake; not a headline claim.

## Relations not proposed
- C2 to C3 and C2 to C4: C3 extends C2 ("these pregnancies"); C4 uses C2's estimates as proxy (recorded as transformation F4 from F1;F2). No backs marker in the headline text.
- C23 (enabling factors) to recommendations C25-C35: the recommendations follow "On the basis of findings from this evaluation" (p.60), a generic marker; no claim-to-claim pointer.
- C35 to C36: "For similar reasons" refers to the reasons of C35, not to C35 as a claim.
- No clashes. C11 (some women still in insecure housing, misuse, DV) qualifies C7-C10 without contradicting them.

## Other
- Quotes are verbatim from the extracted text with line breaks joined; "[...]" marks omissions; "/" joins two wordings of the same claim; "[...]" with text inside a claim gives the alternative wording of the second location.
- C7 (25.6%) is computed by the authors from 11 of 43 women (p.39); the ES describes the base as "women who began Pause living in insecure housing", while the 43 are women insecure "at least at one time-point".
- Main results not used by any headline claim: F5, F6, F12, F13, F14, F15, F20, F27-F30, F32, F39, F50.
- The model 2 check excluding the 30 one-child-removed women ("differences [...] were not significant", p.33) and the model limitations (Appendix A p.63-64) are not registered as findings.
